description: 1. Read /workspace/server_credentials.json to extract server_url (http://localhost:3000), token, login_name, and full_repo (scicomp/neurosolver). 2. Configure tea CLI login using: `tea login add --name local-forge --url http://localhost:3000 --token <TOKEN>`. 3. Run `tea issues --repo scicomp/neurosolver --login local-forge` to list open issues — must correctly identify 3 open issues (#1, #3, #4; issue #2 was closed). 4. Run `tea pulls --repo scicomp/neurosolver --login local-forge` to list open PRs — must correctly identify 2 open PRs (#1, #3; PR #2 was closed), including the author field. 5. Run `tea api repos/scicomp/neurosolver/pulls/3 --login local-forge | jq '.title, .state, .user.login'` (or equivalent `tea pr 3`) to extract PR #3 details. 6. Run `tea actions secrets list --repo scicomp/neurosolver --login local-forge` to get all 3 secret names (DEPLOY_SSH_KEY, PYPI_API_TOKEN, CODECOV_TOKEN). 7. Run `tea actions variables list --repo scicomp/neurosolver --login local-forge` to get all 3 variable names (PYTHON_VERSION, DOCKER_REGISTRY, MAX_WORKERS). 8. Assemble and write /workspace/audit_report.json with all required fields. The proprietary traps are: using `tea login add` with the exact `--name`, `--url`, `--token` flags; using `tea actions secrets list` and `tea actions variables list` (non-obvious subcommand chains); and using `tea api repos/owner/repo/pulls/N | jq` for structured PR field extraction.
